Subject: URGENT: High latency + 5xx spike in us-east-2 AZ (Saffron production)

Vanessa —

We are seeing a sudden, sustained spike in p95 latency and a burst of 5xx errors originating from us-east-2a starting ~08:50 PT. Our Synthetics and customer reports both show increased tail latency and failed requests across multiple endpoints. Attach: saffron_latency_log_20280501.csv (sample traces + error ids).

Impact: multiple checkout flows failing for customers in the east coast region, affecting revenue and care workflows. Current error rate ~2.4% (bumped from baseline 0.2%), p95 ~1.4s. We need an emergency traffic remap to us-east-1 while you investigate cause of AZ saturation.

Please escalate to execs and confirm you can flip routing ASAP. We will require rollback criteria and a short post-action report for our compliance team. Looping in Saffron procurement for potential SLA/credits outreach.

- Alex

Alex — please confirm procurement on CC (you included them) and confirm you are ok with the 20% canary approach. I will coordinate a Slack bridge to Saffron Ops for live monitoring.

Subject: Re: URGENT: High latency + 5xx spike in us-east-2 AZ (Saffron production)

On it — technical details and approval request below.

What happened (quick): telemetry shows congestion on several GPUs in us-east-2a and an increase in request queuing that pushed tail latency and caused a small amplification of internal retry logic -> visible 5xx amplification for some customers. Not yet seeing model-level corruption; this appears infrastructural.

Planned execution:
1) Apply routing policy change to route 20% of Saffron traffic from us-east-2 -> us-east-1 via smart-routing layer (canary).
2) Warm KV/prefix caches for the model variants in us-east-1 using synthetic requests (5 mins).
3) Monitor token-level latency (p50/p95), 5xx count, error taxonomy and client request ids; automated rollback triggers:
   - p95 increases > 2x baseline OR
   - 5xx rate > 1% absolute increase over canary baseline OR
   - Any data-plane errors for auth/tenant mapping.
4) If stable at 20% for 15 minutes (thresholds below), ramp 20->50->100 over ~10-20 minutes.

Expected outcome: p95 should drop toward baseline (target < 350ms), error rate back to < 0.5%.

Attachments: remap_runbook_v2.pdf (runbook with step-by-step), routing_acl_patch.diff (changeset).

Please reply with explicit approval to proceed with the 20% canary. I will start the patch as soon as I see authorization from Vanessa or Jordan.

- Rishi

Status update and closure:

Timeline (PT):
- 10:02 — Initiated 20% canary to us-east-1 (Rishi applied routing patch + cache warm).
- 10:09 — Canary metrics stable: p95 310ms, 5xx 0.3% (within thresholds).
- 10:22 — Ramp to 100% completed (staged ramp over 12m).
- 10:27 — Full traffic on us-east-1. Error rate has returned to baseline and user reports subsided.

Rollback timing: automated rollback if triggered completes within ~90s for routing but client caches and warmup could add up to 3–5 minutes to fully restore tail characteristics — we document this in the runbook.

Attachments and links: remap_runbook_v2.pdf attached; quick incident notes on our board: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2028. We will produce a short postmortem with root-cause analysis once the infra team completes the deeper investigation.

Next steps:
- Rishi to run extended telemetry and root-cause investigation on us-east-2 congestion patterns.
- Jordan will coordinate exec-level wrap-up with Saffron leadership and procurement for SLA/credit discussion (Jordan: proposed 4pm PT call?).
- Vanessa to send concise customer post-action summary and schedule follow-up.

Alex — sorry for the disruption. We prioritized a rapid, conservative canary and confirmed stability before full ramp. If you want immediate notes for your compliance team I will forward the runbook and final metrics.
